channel.title: MOONX guides
channel.description: Plain-English guides to prediction markets and Polymarket: how prices and payouts work, fees, resolution, selling early, and how to use MOONX.

item.title: What is a prediction market? A plain-English guide
item.description: A prediction market lets you buy Yes or No on a real question. Here is how prices, shares and payouts work, with simple examples and the risks.

item.title: How does Polymarket work? Shares, prices and payouts
item.description: How Polymarket works, step by step: Yes and No shares, the order book, the price you see versus the price you pay, minimums, settlement and apps.

item.title: Prediction market odds: how a price becomes a payout
item.description: Turn any Polymarket price into a probability, a payout multiple, decimal and American odds. A full table, worked examples and what fees change.

item.title: Polymarket fees explained, with real numbers
item.description: Polymarket's taker fee by category, the formula, what it costs in cents on a real trade, when there is no fee, and what MOONX adds on top.

item.title: How Polymarket markets are resolved, and what happens in a dispute
item.description: Who decides the result of a Polymarket market: the UMA oracle, the $750 bond, the 2-hour challenge window, disputes, votes, and 50-50 outcomes.

item.title: Selling before the result: take profit or cut a loss on Polymarket
item.description: Yes, you can sell Polymarket shares any time before a market ends. How the sale price works, when to take profit, when to cut a loss, with examples.

item.title: Long shots on Polymarket: why 5¢ pays 20x, and why most never do
item.description: How cheap Polymarket shares pay 10x, 20x or 100x, how often they win, the long-shot bias, fees at low prices, and a sane way to play moonshots.

item.title: Prediction markets vs sports betting: what is actually different
item.description: Bookmaker odds versus a market price, who is on the other side, selling before the end, fees versus margin, and which one suits you. A neutral comparison.

item.title: Multi-outcome markets on Polymarket: elections, awards and "Other"
item.description: How Polymarket markets with many answers work: one Yes/No market per candidate, why prices add up to about $1, negative risk, and the trap of "Other".

item.title: Polymarket glossary: every word you will see, explained
item.description: Plain definitions of the words you meet on Polymarket and MOONX: shares, bid, ask, spread, maker, taker, resolution, UMA, negative risk, pUSD and more.

item.title: Your first trade on MOONX, step by step
item.description: From email sign-up to your first Yes or No: creating your account, setting up your wallet, adding money by card, trading, selling and withdrawing.

item.title: Your MOONX wallet: who holds the keys, and what you must keep
item.description: How the MOONX wallet works: keys made on your device, one backup file and a password, a PIN per device, switching devices, and what nobody can recover.

item.title: Earn with MOONX: your crew and trades taken from your posts
item.description: How you earn on MOONX: 25% of our fee on your crew's trades for life, 25% when someone trades from your post, how both add up, and when you get paid.

item.title: Polymarket copy trading: follow a trade, or take the other side
item.description: Can you copy Polymarket traders? What public wallets show, why your price differs from theirs, the traps of copying blindly, and how the MOONX feed works.

item.title: What is MOONX? The social app to trade on Polymarket
item.description: MOONX (moonx.fi) is a social app to trade on Polymarket: a feed of real trades, Yes or No in a few taps, card payments and a wallet only you control.

item.title: Are prediction markets accurate?
item.description: Often, yes. Studies find market forecasts fairly accurate and often closer than polls, but cheap long shots tend to win less often than their price says.

item.title: Can you use MOONX on your phone?
item.description: Yes. MOONX works in your phone's browser at moonx.fi and inside Telegram as a Mini App, and one wallet works across your phone and computer.

item.title: Can you lose more than you bet on Polymarket?
item.description: No. You pay for Polymarket shares up front and a losing share is worth $0, so the most one trade can cost you is what you paid, fees included.

item.title: Can you use Polymarket with a credit or debit card?
item.description: Polymarket's deposit guides describe crypto transfers. MOONX lets you pay by card, mobile wallet or bank transfer, with the partner's fee shown first.

item.title: Do you need crypto to use Polymarket?
item.description: Polymarket trades only in pUSD, a dollar token on Polygon, so your money must become a digital dollar. You don't need to own crypto first if an app takes cards.

item.title: Do you pay taxes on Polymarket winnings?
item.description: It depends on where you live. Rules differ by country, so keep a record of every trade and check locally. MOONX gives no tax advice and doesn't report for you.

item.title: How do Polymarket sports markets work?
item.description: Polymarket sports markets let you buy Yes or No on a result, like who wins a match. Winning shares pay $1. How rules, resolution and the 0.05 fee work.

item.title: How do you make money on Polymarket?
item.description: Two ways. Hold a share that wins and it pays $1, or sell it to another trader for more than you paid. Both need the market to prove you right.

item.title: How long does Polymarket take to pay out?
item.description: About 2 hours after a result is proposed if nobody disputes it, about 4 to 6 days if it's disputed. On MOONX the money lands minutes to hours later.

item.title: How do you read a Polymarket chart?
item.description: A Polymarket chart shows a share's price over time, which reads as the market's implied probability. Here is what jumps, flat lines and drifts mean.

item.title: How do you sell a position on MOONX?
item.description: Tap Eject on your position: MOONX sells at the best price on the book and the money goes back to your wallet. On a thin market it can fill lower or partly.

item.title: How do you withdraw money from MOONX?
item.description: Add an address that accepts USDC on Polygon to your Payout Wallets list, then withdraw with your PIN. No withdrawal fee, and MOONX pays the network fee.

item.title: Is MOONX safe?
item.description: MOONX is non-custodial: your keys stay on your device, so MOONX can't move or freeze your money. What that protects, and what can still go wrong.

item.title: Is Polymarket safe?
item.description: What can go wrong on Polymarket, from smart contract bugs and disputed results to thin markets, lost wallet access and scams posing as apps.

item.title: What are the fees on MOONX?
item.description: MOONX charges 1% of the trade value when you buy and when you sell. No fee at resolution or to withdraw, and gas is paid. Polymarket's fee applies too.

item.title: What is the minimum bet on Polymarket?
item.description: The floor is often 5 shares, and an instant buy also needs about $1. So the smallest trade is just over $1 up to 20¢, then 5 times the price above it.

item.title: What are gas fees?
item.description: Gas fees are what a blockchain charges to process a transaction, paid in its own token. On Polygon that token is POL. On MOONX, MOONX pays them for you.

item.title: What are Polymarket rewards and rebates?
item.description: Polymarket runs three programs that pay traders back: liquidity rewards and maker rebates for posted orders, and a tiered taker rebate. How each works.

item.title: What are Polymarket Up or Down markets?
item.description: Up or Down markets ask if a crypto price ends a short window higher or lower. Chainlink prices settle them, and a tie counts as Up. Fees and an example.

item.title: What blockchain is Polymarket on?
item.description: Polymarket runs on Polygon, chain ID 137. What that means for you, which network to send money on, what gas is, and why MOONX users never need POL.

item.title: What does the percentage mean on Polymarket?
item.description: The percentage is the price of a Yes share. 64% means Yes costs about 64¢, pays $1 if right, and traders put the chance near 64%. Not a promise.

item.title: What happens if a Polymarket market is unclear?
item.description: Unclear markets are judged on their written rules. Polymarket may add a clarification, and if no answer fits, the market resolves 50-50 at $0.50 a share.

item.title: What happens if you lose your MOONX backup file?
item.description: If you lose the backup file or its password, the wallet and its money are lost for good, and MOONX keeps no copy. How to store both safely today.

item.title: What is a combo on Polymarket?
item.description: A Polymarket combo joins two or more outcomes into one Yes or No position. Yes pays only if every leg wins. Market makers quote the price on request.

item.title: What is a limit order on Polymarket?
item.description: A limit order sets the worst price you accept. It fills now if the book allows, or waits until someone takes it. Makers pay no fee on Polymarket.

item.title: What is a non-custodial wallet?
item.description: A non-custodial wallet is one where only you hold the keys: no wallet provider can move or freeze your money, or recover it. How MOONX applies it.

item.title: What is a Polymarket builder?
item.description: A Polymarket builder is an app that sends its users' orders to Polymarket with a builder code, so their trades count toward its volume. MOONX is one.

item.title: What is a shot on MOONX?
item.description: A shot is MOONX's word for a trade: a position on one outcome of a Polymarket market. Each share pays $1 if you're right, and you can sell it anytime.

item.title: What is expected value in prediction markets?
item.description: Expected value is what a trade returns on average. Per share, it's your chance times $1, minus the price, minus fees. Worked examples with real fees.

item.title: What is liquidity on Polymarket?
item.description: Liquidity is how many shares you can buy or sell near the current price. It comes from limit orders waiting in the book, and Polymarket pays to attract it.

item.title: What is pUSD on Polymarket?
item.description: pUSD is Polymarket's dollar token on Polygon, backed by USDC. Every trade and every payout on Polymarket is settled in it.

item.title: What is slippage on Polymarket?
item.description: Slippage is when a market order fills at worse prices than the best one shown, because it uses up several levels of the order book. Here is the math.

item.title: What is the spread on Polymarket?
item.description: The spread is the gap between the best bid and the best ask. It is what you lose if you buy and sell at once, and it hits cheap shares hardest.

item.title: What is UMA on Polymarket?
item.description: UMA is the oracle that settles most Polymarket markets. Anyone can propose a result with a $750 bond or dispute it, and UMA token holders vote on disputes.

item.title: What is volume on Polymarket?
item.description: Volume is how much has been traded on a Polymarket market over a period. It shows activity, not how much money is at stake or who is right.
